title: The Information Lattice Model: Entropic Permeability, Emergent Gravity, and the Holographic Structure of the Brane–Bulk Interface
content: We introduce the Information Lattice Model (ILM), a theoretical framework in the braneworld tradition in which the brane–bulk system is represented as a stratified informational graph whose inter-layer link capacity is governed by a permeability function Π(y) = 1 + ε exp(−λ|y|/ℓₚₗ). The dimensionless parameter ε is identified with the ratio of bulk-to-brane entanglement entropy flux via the Ryu–Takayanagi formula, connecting the model to the Bekenstein–Hawking entropy bound and the AdS/CFT correspondence. This identification is presented as a conceptual proposal in the tradition of framework papers from Kaluza–Klein to Verlinde’s entropic gravity, ahead of full formal derivation. The permeability function modifies the Randall–Sundrum warp factor, introducing an additional entropic dilution of the effective gravitational coupling beyond geometric warping alone. Within this framework, the ILM may offer a unified phenomenological perspective on the hierarchy problem, the black hole information paradox, and the possible role of sub-brane entropic degrees of freedom as an effective dark matter component. Two falsifiable predictions are identified: a positive correlation between dimensionless radiated energy excess Δerad and total merger mass Mₜₒₜₐₗ in binary black hole systems, testable via stacked regression of the GWTC-3 catalogue and decisive single-event tests with LISA; and a non-linear deviation in quantum decoherence rates near lattice saturation, testable with ion traps and superconducting qubits. A full Bayesian treatment of Prediction I and derivation of the ILM action from a variational entropic principle are presented as priorities for future work.
